subject: Vendor onboarding: vendor landing page vs email fallback for invoice ingestion
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor onboarding: invoice submission options and PO handling

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this. We're kicking off finance onboarding for Acme (x-subsidiaries EU/US). Before we register in your portal we have a couple of constraints from our AP team:

- Multi-PO invoices: sometimes a single invoice ties to 2-3 POs (different projects). Can your intake support multiple PO numbers per invoice? Do they need to be line-level or can they sit at invoice header?
- VAT and multi-currency: we need VAT detail lines when billing EU entities. Is there a template for VAT breakdown per line?
- Pilot preferences: for the first 60 days we prefer a simple email-based submit (SMTP) — lower integration effort. We can move to a portal later.

Can you share your recommended path (vendor landing/portal vs email fallback), the minimal CSV template for invoices, and any subject/filename conventions we must follow for idempotency/PO mapping?

Tom
Finance Ops - Acme Corp
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: invoice submission options and PO handling

Tom — thanks, great context. Short answer: both paths are supported; portal (vendor landing) is preferred for production, email fallback for short-term pilots. Details and tradeoffs below. Attached: vendor-landing-form_v1.pdf and sample-invoice-template.csv.

1) Vendor landing / portal (recommended)
- Vendors register via a landing page; we issue a Vendor ID and pre-populate your profile (tax IDs, default currency, country/regional routing).
- Portal ingestion includes structured fields for invoice header-level PO and line-level PO. If you want to associate multiple POs to one invoice we recommend mapping them to line items (we support up to 10 PO references across lines). Portal also surfaces a VAT breakdown per line.
- Benefits: deterministic parsing, automatic ACK webhook (within 30–60s), built-in idempotency keys, and per-route SLA routing by region.

2) Email fallback (acceptable for pilots)
- Supported: PDF invoices attached, CSV payloads, or invoice embedded in email body. For best mapping, use our subject convention:
  Subject: REDWOOD-VID:<VENDORID> INVOICE:<INVOICE_NUMBER> DATE:<YYYYMMDD>
- If you don't yet have a Vendor ID, use: REDWOOD-VID:ACME-PILOT INVOICE:<INVOICE_NUMBER>
- Filename convention (helps automated PO stamping): <INVOICE_NUMBER>|PO:<PO1>,<PO2>|CUR:<ISO_CUR>.pdf
- Idempotency: include X-Idempotency: <random-token> in the email headers (or include token in subject). If omitted we fallback to checksuming the attachment which can introduce duplicate risk.

3) VAT and multi-currency handling
- VAT: portal supports explicit VAT line per line-item and invoice-level VAT summary. For email CSV use the attached sample where columns include: line_description, qty, unit_price, currency, tax_rate, tax_amount, po_number. If a line needs multiple PO references, put them comma-separated in po_number.
- Currency: invoice-level currency determines payment currency; line-level currency is allowed but will trigger a reconciliation flag and human review.

4) PO placement recommendations
- Best: PO at line-level (cleanest accounting). Acceptable: invoice header-level PO if invoice maps to one PO only. For multi-PO invoices, header-level will not reliably map to multiple GL codes without line mapping.

5) ACKs and SLA
- Portal: webhook ACK + human validation flag; email: we attempt automated ACK (email reply) within 15–120 minutes depending on parser confidence. For pilot, expect a manual review window.

6) Quick sample (CSV) — see attached sample-invoice-template.csv (excerpt):
- invoice_number,invoice_date,currency,line_description,qty,unit_price,po_number,tax_rate,tax_amount
- INV-20270701,2027-07-01,USD,Consulting retainer,1,5000.00,PO-12345,0.00,0.00
- INV-20270701,2027-07-01,USD,Dev hours,20,150.00,PO-12346,0.00,0.00
- INV-20270701,2027-07-01,EUR,EU VAT reclaim,1,0.00,PO-12346,20.00,300.00

Next steps I propose: we enable ACME pilot with email fallback (REDWOOD-VID:ACME-PILOT) and shared subject/filename convention. Jordan will coordinate procurement acceptance checklist and region routing. After 45 days we expect to flip to portal/landing for ongoing production.

Let me know if you'd like us to provision a temporary Vendor ID today.

— Stephanie
Procurement Onboarding, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Finance <payables@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: vendor landing page vs email fallback for invoice ingestion

On Mon, Jul 19, 2027 at 11:03 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Tom — thanks, great context. Short answer: both paths are supported; portal (vendor landing) is preferred for production, email fallback for short-term pilots.

Thanks, that helps. A couple of clarifying points from our AP lead:
- Can your parser reliably handle mixed-currency lines (we sometimes invoice USD services + EUR VAT lines on one file)? You mentioned it flags for review — how frequent is that in practice?
- For the early pilot we won't embed PO numbers at line-level; can we put a header-level field with a mapping file after submission? Our ERP team prefers to do PO-to-line mapping on their side.

Also, we'd like the ACK email to include the parsed PO list and an idempotency token so our ERP can confirm receipt programmatically. If you can include that in the ACK payload (subject or reply body) it's perfect.

Tom
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: vendor landing page vs email fallback for invoice ingestion

Tom — looping in confirmation/next steps. Short replies to the asks:

- Mixed-currency: parser accepts mixed-currency lines but flags ~8–12% of those invoices for manual QA in our experience (depends on currency mismatch patterns). We'll surface the flag in the ACK.
- Header-level PO + post-submission mapping: acceptable for the pilot. We'll capture header PO(s) and include a parsed PO list in the ACK; however if you need guaranteed GL-level mapping we should move to line-level mapping in the portal.
- ACK payload: yes — we'll include: parsed_po_list, idempotency_token, vendor_id (temporary if used), parser_confidence (high/medium/low) in the reply email body.

Action items:
1) Stephanie: provision temporary Vendor ID (ACME-PILOT) and enable email ingestion + subject/filename pattern.
2) Karthik: attach procurement-acceptance-checklist.xlsx and confirm SLA and regional routing config (EU VAT path).
3) Tom: send a sample pilot invoice using the attached sample-invoice-template.csv and include an X-Idempotency header if possible.

We will stand up the pilot today once Stephanie confirms the Vendor ID.

Thanks — Jordan
Head of Go-to-Market Ops, Redwood Inference
